pr_title: Fix #520: Enable caching + reusing schemas across routes, support for $refs
pr_body:
This resolves #520, but still has a couple open discussion points:

1. Should the public API include `addSchema`, or should users go through `options.ajv.schemas` to seed it?
2. Should the public API include `addKeyword`?

Additionally, couple questions that came up during implementation:

1. ~Should this expose the AJV Typescript dependency?~ No, better to hide the AJV dependency if it changes later
2. ~Style note: what approach suits this codebase best around the reusable helper 'MapCache' that I've added? Should this be in the same file as the validator? Should it be a class? etc.~ Better to be a function. Will leave as is since it's now shared across a couple files.
3. ~How many versions back in Node should I run the tests? I tested it with `v8.0.0`~ Should be tested back to v4.5
4. Is it preferred to squash all the commits or leave them individually?

Feedback very welcome!
pr_comments: I think that just answered how many versions back of Node I need to go. 😄

I would say that yes, we don’t want to be exposing anything of AJV, as we might want to swap it for something else in the future.

However, It think that storing schema references and providing an integration with fast-json-stringify should be in scope.

Alright finally got some time to come back and fix my initial issues.

The PR has been updated with the following changes:

1. Support for Node back to v4.5
2. New `setSchemaResolver` that mirrors the behavior of `setSchemaCompiler` is used to resolve references - this cleans up some of the stuff I was pushing onto schema compiler and makes it easier to use with a custom validation library
3. `getSchema` now goes through the cache to get the schema
4. Removed AJV dependency from typescript interface based on discussion here
5. Updated documentation + typescript examples

Thanks for the constructive feedback - I'm much happier with this PR than when I first submitted it. Please let me know if there's anything else I can improve.

Can you please remove:

* [ ] `fastify.validate`
* [ ] `fastify.getStringify`
* [ ] `fastify.stringify`

I do not think they are needed for this PR.
I've updated this PR to handle the feedback + merged with the latest in master.
I’m not 100% in agreement with that change @allevo. I would prefer to discuss that in a follow-up PR!
Updated with merge changes + PR fixes! Thanks for taking a look at this.
Good work, I think this is ready to land!
@nwoltman thanks for catching that! I've added a test + the documentation you wanted. Let me know if there's anything further you'd expect to see.
Can you rebase on top of master? It is now conflicting.
Merged with the latest from master

Thanks @dougrich! Just a couple nits and one more important thing.

These functions:
```ts
/**
 * Sets a resolver to use when trying to resolve schemas
 */
setSchemaResolver(resolver: SchemaResolver): FastifyInstance<HttpServer, HttpRequest, HttpResponse>

/**
 * Adds a schema
 */
addSchema(schema: Object, keyRef?: string): void

/**
 * Gets a function to validate using a saved schema
 */
getSchema(keyRef: string): ValidateFunction
```

should be documented in `docs/Server-Methods.md`.

@nwoltman Added the stubs in the `docs/Server-Methods.md`; like the documentation for `setSchemaCompiler` I've pointed them to the documentation I'd already written in `docs/Validation-and-Serialization.md`. Let me know if you'd prefer something more verbose.

issue_context.title: Deeper access to internal AJV?
comments:
I think we need a better story on how to reuse schemas across the library.
Would you like to send a PR?
If you want to have different serialization schemas you can also use [`any-schema-you-like`](https://github.com/fastify/any-schema-you-like) :)

PR #528 is open with the API interface + behavior I proposed above.

I mentioned two open discussion points that need to be resolved before merging in: @zenflow's ask for the `addKeyword` functionality and an open question on if the public API should expose `addSchema` or if all schemas should be passed in through `options.ajv.schemas`.

I'm personally preferential to `addSchema` as that means it'd be possible to add schemas alongside routes or in plugins, but I'm fine with either way in the long run.

I'm not sure what the best approach with `addKeyword` is, since I've not personally needed to use it. I see @zenflow's use case but looking back at the discussion in some of those previous issues I'm not sure how much of AJV's api you want to let flow through before just exposing `fastify.ajv` directly.

Please let me know if you have any feedback on the PR.

EDIT: added additional use case for why we'd want `addSchema` as a first-class part of the API.

Another use case. I typically add an `xregexp` keyword to AJV to validate with [`XRegExp`](http://xregexp.com/), so that I get classes of Unicode characters, which the JSON Schema spec [does not include](http://json-schema.org/latest/json-schema-validation.html#rfc.section.4.3).

I typically do this to ensure client strings are clean: `XRegExp("^[^\\p{C}\\p{Zl}\\p{Zp}]+$")`.

review_comments: Can we avoid caching the resolved function completely? I mean, this will only be executed at startup time, and it looks like a premature optimization to cache them.
I think this may be related to #611 so the `opts.schemaResolver` part isn't necessary.

Oh wait, I just saw the _"you can pass it in either on route options or through `setSchemaResolver`"_ note in the documentation. In that case, you'll need to add the `schemaResolver` option after [this line](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/889530b38c36833b30d3a7db6c0a83c493e85c6c/fastify.js#L378), a test to make sure the option works, and also documentation for the option to the [Route docs](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/docs/Routes.md#full-declaration).
Can you avoid copying the array for the "happy-path" case? `cache.get(id)` should not have the array copied.
